alerts.title: Rising creatinine on TDF in pregnancy
alerts.message: TDF is associated with renal toxicity including proximal tubular dysfunction and declining eGFR. Patient's creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.1 mg/dL within 10 weeks of starting TDF, with eGFR now 78 mL/min/1.73m². Pregnancy normally increases creatinine clearance, so a rising creatinine during pregnancy is particularly concerning. Phosphate remains normal at 3.8 mg/dL and urinalysis shows no protein or glucose, which argues against significant proximal tubular damage. However, the upward trend warrants close monitoring. Non-drug causes such as dehydration or pre-eclampsia should also be considered, though BP is normal and no oedema is present.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat creatinine and eGFR within 2-4 weeks. If creatinine continues to rise, consider switching TDF to TAF. Monitor phosphate and urinalysis periodically.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring frequency in pregnancy
alerts.message: Guidelines specify viral load monitoring at 6 months after ART initiation then every 12 months for adults, but every 3 months for pregnant and lactating women. Patient initiated ART 10 weeks ago, so the 6-month VL is not yet due. However, after that initial 6-month test, VL should be repeated every 3 months during pregnancy and breastfeeding rather than annually. Current VL of 89 copies/mL is suppressed and treatment response is excellent. The clinician should document a VL monitoring schedule aligned with pregnancy-specific intervals.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule next viral load at 6 months post-ART initiation, then every 3 months during pregnancy and breastfeeding per pregnancy-specific monitoring guidelines.

alerts.title: Missing TPT screening and plan
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend initiating TB preventive treatment (TPT) after 3 months on ART for newly initiating patients. Patient started ART 10 weeks ago and will reach the 3-month threshold soon. No TB screening or TPT plan is documented. TB screening is especially important in pregnancy given increased vulnerability. No TB symptoms are reported, which would support TPT eligibility once the 3-month mark is reached. The clinician should assess TB status and plan TPT initiation at the next visit.

evidence.recommended_action: Screen for TB at next visit. If no active TB disease, initiate TPT prophylaxis as patient will have completed 3 months on ART.

alerts.title: No clinician assessment or plan documented
alerts.message: No assessment or plan was documented for this visit. Given pregnancy on TDF/3TC/DTG with rising creatinine, haemoglobin of 10.8 g/dL, and approaching TPT eligibility, a documented plan addressing renal monitoring, anaemia evaluation, and TB prevention is needed. The patient is also due for routine antenatal care coordination. Hb of 10.8 g/dL may reflect physiological haemodilution of pregnancy or iron deficiency; ferrous sulfate is already prescribed.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a comprehensive plan addressing renal monitoring, anaemia follow-up, TPT screening at 3 months, and antenatal care coordination.
